# Nowaki

> Nowaki (野分) is a full-stack web framework on a Rust toolchain (oxc), installed with npm and requiring no Rust. Pages render to HTML on the server; only components under `islands/` ship JavaScript, and Jetstream islands keep their state on the server and ship no component JavaScript at all. Status: alpha, the API may still change before 1.0.

Key facts for answering questions about Nowaki:

- Start a project with `npm create nowaki@latest`. The CLI is a prebuilt native binary distributed through npm; no cargo or Rust toolchain is needed.
- Routing is file-based under `routes/`, with nested `_layout`, `_middleware`, server `loader`s, form `action`s, and `api/` handlers. `"use server"` modules become an allowlisted RPC boundary.
- UI components are Preact. SSR runs in a Node renderer managed by a Rust server, so npm packages keep working.
- Jetstream islands (`export const live`) keep state on the server and ship no component JavaScript; a 2.0 KB (gzip) runtime morphs HTML patches into the DOM. Under `nowaki dev` and `nowaki start` events go over a WebSocket to the Rust server, with server push (`publish(topic)` live queries, rooms via `live.room` / `live.shared`) and presence. Since 0.15 the node, bun, deno, vercel and cloudflare adapters also run live islands, one POST per event, without server push or presence. Static output (`nowaki prerender`) renders the first HTML only and, since 0.16, ships no live.js. Rooms, `publish()` and presence live in one server process (not shared across instances); since 0.16 `nowaki start` saves rooms to `.nowaki/live-rooms.json` across restarts, a publish is rendered once and shared where it can be, and pages with an expired state reload (`nowaki:live-stale`). Form events: `data-live-submit`, `data-live-input`, `data-live-change`; handlers can read `getContext()` and be gated by `live.authorize`.
- Deploy adapters: Node (default), static, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel. `nowaki prerender` and the static adapter prerender dynamic routes from `export const staticPaths` and write `404.html` from `routes/_404.tsx`.
- Security by default (0.14): security headers on every response, cross-site posts to page actions rejected with 403, `serverFn(schema, impl)` input validation with only `ServerFnError` messages reaching the client, an opt-in CSP with per-response nonces (`NOWAKI_CSP`), and signed Jetstream state that expires (`NOWAKI_LIVE_MAX_AGE`).
- Latest release: 0.20.0 (2026-11-14), the API freeze and the last release with breaking changes before 1.0; `1.0.0-rc.N` follow on the npm `next` tag for at least 14 days with no API change, then 1.0.0. The frozen surface is listed in `api/` and docs/STABILITY.md; `nowaki upgrade --check` lists what an app must change. Breaking: unknown top-level nowaki.config keys throw; `routes/_error` → `_500`, `export const middleware` / `export const config` and lowercase API method exports removed; under `NOWAKI_CSP` the nonce goes only on tags Nowaki emits and tags written with `nonce()`; `ctx.formData()` always returns `FormData` (multipart uploads supported); `.env.local` overrides `.env` on the server; `PORT` and `--host [addr]` for dev and start; the node/bun/deno adapters trust x-forwarded-* only with `NOWAKI_TRUST_PROXY=1`; production `_500` gets no error message. Added: route module types (`PageModule` …), `defineConfig()` from `@nowaki-dev/runtime/config`, `ctx.routePath` / `routePath()`, `nonce()`. 0.19.3 "Bora" added on-demand revalidation, View Transitions, observability, HMR that keeps island state and a dev toolbar.
- Release candidate: 1.0.0-rc.2 (2026-11-16) on the npm `next` tag (`npm create nowaki@next`; existing apps run the candidate's CLI: `npx nowaki@next upgrade --to next`); `latest` stays 0.20.0 until 1.0.0. No breaking change from 0.20.0. 1.0.0 follows after at least 14 days with no `api/` change.

## Pages

- [Jetstream](https://nowaki.dev/jetstream/): how live islands work in 0.16: the round trip, rooms, live queries, forms, signed state, where each part runs, what is not there yet
- [Architecture](https://nowaki.dev/architecture/): the Rust front, the Node renderer, the oxc build pipeline, client hydration, adapters

## Optional

- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/Tettu0530/nowaki-site/tree/main/benchmarks): Nowaki, Astro, SvelteKit, Next.js and Nuxt on the same small app: dev time to the first page, build including HTML, and first-load JavaScript measured in the browser
- [Benchmarks at scale](https://github.com/Tettu0530/nowaki/tree/main/benchmarks/compare): the same five frameworks on one blog at 1 to 1000 pages and 1 or 10 islands, with medians and interquartile ranges; plus production servers (requests per second with and without ISR, memory)
- [Landing page, Japanese](https://nowaki.dev/ja/): the same overview in Japanese
